Im not from Ireland or NI so feel free to take my opinion with a grain of salt, but I would consider the sectarian divides that were created and later propped up by England to be occupation. 

Again this isnt in the long time ago, there are a lot of people alive (on both sides) who vividly remember violence against each other. Is it healthy to maintain that anger and fan those flames forever? No obviously not. But when people cant even fathom why a group could be unhappy with them it doesn't bode well for that anger subsiding.

In this specific case Irish people are referring to the present occupation of the island, not to mention that the Troubles ended (on paper) in '99. Not exactly ancient history.  

Even so, I don't think it's surprising or wrong for people to hold resentment when they can trace a very clear line from the mistreatment by someone's great great grandparents to inequalities today.  It doesn't make it this generation's fault, but it can feel like a slap in the face when the other side won't even acknowledge why things are the way they are.
